subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the Mr of sodium hydroxide, NaOH? (Ar: Na=23, O=16, H=1)
Why must aluminium oxide be molten during the extraction of aluminium?
options: So the ions are free to move and carry charge
questions.explain: The aluminium oxide must be molten so its ions can move and be electrolysed.

questions.q: In the electrolysis of dilute sulfuric acid, what forms at the cathode?
questions.explain: Hydrogen ions are discharged at the cathode, producing hydrogen gas.

questions.q: In the electrolysis of aqueous sodium sulfate, what forms at the cathode?
questions.explain: Sodium is more reactive than hydrogen, so hydrogen is discharged at the cathode.

questions.q: Iron is extracted from its ore in the blast furnace by reduction with which substance?
questions.explain: Iron is less reactive than carbon, so carbon reduces iron oxide to iron in the blast furnace.

questions.q: How many moles are in 36 g of water, H2O? (Mr = 18)
questions.explain: moles = mass/Mr = 36/18 = 2 mol.

questions.q: What is observed when a small piece of sodium is added to water?
options: It fizzes, moves on the surface and releases hydrogen
It turns the water bright blue
questions.explain: Sodium reacts vigorously with water, fizzing as it produces hydrogen gas and sodium hydroxide.

questions.q: A solution contains 20 g of solute in 0.5 dm³. What is its concentration in g/dm³?
questions.explain: concentration = mass/volume = 20/0.5 = 40 g/dm³.

questions.q: In electrolysis, what is the charge on the cathode?
questions.explain: The cathode is the negative electrode.

questions.q: Why does oiling or greasing iron tools help prevent rusting?
options: It keeps out water and oxygen
It makes the iron more reactive
questions.explain: A barrier of oil keeps water and oxygen away from the iron surface.

questions.q: Why is aluminium extracted by electrolysis rather than reduction with carbon?
options: Aluminium is less reactive than carbon
Aluminium does not form an ore
Aluminium is more reactive than carbon
questions.explain: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon, so carbon cannot reduce its oxide and electrolysis must be used.

questions.q: What is the Mr of carbon dioxide, CO2? (Ar: C=12, O=16)
Balance: N2 + ?H2 → 2NH3. What number goes in front of H2?
questions.explain: 3H2 gives 6 H atoms, matching 2NH3 (6 H), and N2 gives 2 N.

questions.q: Which two substances are both needed for iron to rust?
questions.explain: Rusting of iron requires both water and oxygen to be present.

questions.q: At the anode during electrolysis of aqueous sodium chloride, the product is:
questions.explain: When a halide ion is present, the halogen (chlorine) is produced at the anode rather than oxygen.

questions.q: Which electrode do positive ions (cations) move towards?
questions.explain: Cations are positive and are attracted to the negative cathode.

questions.q: Which half equation correctly represents what happens at the cathode for copper ions?
questions.explain: At the cathode, copper ions gain electrons (reduction): Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu.

questions.q: For an ionic compound to act as an electrolyte it must be:
questions.explain: Ions must be free to move, which only happens when the ionic compound is molten or in solution.

questions.q: Which metal will displace copper from copper sulfate solution?
questions.explain: Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from copper sulfate solution.

questions.q: Why is aluminium extracted by electrolysis rather than by reduction with carbon?
options: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon
Carbon does not exist in nature
questions.explain: Aluminium is too reactive to be displaced by carbon, so electrolysis is required.

questions.q: At the anode, what happens to negative ions?
questions.explain: Negative ions lose electrons at the anode, which is oxidation.

questions.q: What is electrolysis?
questions.explain: Electrolysis uses an electric current to break down (decompose) a compound.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE (9–1) Chemistry (1CH0) specification; Separate Chemistry 1
